चैतन्य चैतन्य, अम्, n. (fr. चेतन), intel-
ligence, mental perception, feeling, consciousness,
sense, sensation, soul, spirit, the deity considered as
the essence of all being and source of all sensation;
(अस्), m., N. of a modern reformer of the Vaiṣṇava
faith, who is regarded in Bengal as an Ava-tāra of
Kṛṣṇa; he was born about 1484 A. D., and his
life is described by Kṛṣṇa-dāsa in a work named
Caitanya-caraṇāmṛta or Caitanya-caritāmṛta.
—चै-
तन्य-चन्द्रोदय (˚र-उद्˚), अम्, n. ‘the moon-
rise of Caitanya,’ title of a play.
—चैतन्य-युक्त,
अस्, आ, अम्, endowed with consciousness, sentient.
—चैतन्यामृत (˚य-अम्˚), अम्, n. title of a
grammar.

चैतसिक चैतसिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. चेतस्), re-
lating to the mind or heart.

चैतिक चैतिक, आस्, m. pl. (fr. 2. चैत्य?),
N. of a Buddhist school.

चैत्तिक, अस्, ई, अम्, mental, intellectual, belonging
to thought.

चैत्त चैत्त, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. चित्त), mental,
belonging to thought or intelligence.

चैत्य 1. चैत्य, अस्, m. (fr. 5. चित् or 2. चिति),
the individual soul.

चैत्य 2. चैत्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. चिता), relating
to a funeral pile or grave; (अस्, अम्), m. n. a
monument, a tombstone, a column &c. erected in
memory of some deceased person or on the site of a
funeral pile; a pile of stones forming a landmark
or boundary; a sacred tree, a religious fig-tree &c.
growing in or near a village and held in veneration
by the villagers; a place of sacrifice or religious
worship, an altar, a shed kept for sacrifices &c.; a
sacred building peculiar to the Jainas, a Jaina temple;
a Jaina or Buddhist image; (अस्), m., N. of a moun-
tain.
—चैत्य-तरु, उस्, m. a fig-tree standing on a
sacred spot.
—चैत्य-द्रु, उस्, m., N. of the Ficus
Religiosa [cf. अश्वत्थ]; a large tree in a village.
—चैत्य-द्रुम, अस्, m. = चैत्य-तरु.
—चैत्य-
पाल, अस्, m. the guardian of a sanctuary.
—चैत्य-
मुख, अस्, m. an hermit's water-pot.
—चैत्य-
यज्ञ, अस्, m. a sacrificial ceremony performed at
monuments.
—चैत्य-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, containing
a sanctuary.
—चैत्य-वृक्ष, अस्, m. a fig-tree
standing on a sacred spot; the tree Ficus Religiosa.
—चैत्य-शैल, आस्, m. pl., N. of a Buddhist school;
[cf. चैतिक.]
—चैत्य-स्थान, अम्, n. a place made
sacred by a monument or a temple.

चैत्यक, अस्, m., N. of one of the five moun-
tains surrounding the town Giri-vraja.

चैत्र चैत्र, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. चित्र and चित्रा),
made of the tree called Citra or Citrā; (अस्), m.,
N. of a spring month or the month in which the
full moon stands in the constellation Citrā (March-
April); N. of the sixth year in the cycle of Jupiter;
a Buddhist or Jaina religious mendicant; a common
N. for a man, used like Deva-datta as a general desig-
nation for any person; a metronymic (from Citrā) for
the son of Budha and grandfather of Su-ratha; one of
the seven ranges of mountains dividing the continent
into divisions or Varṣas; (ई), f., scil. पौर्णमासी,
the day of full moon in the month Caitra and the
sacrifice offered on that day; (अम्), n. a monument
erected to the dead, a column or block of wood, a
tree &c. so considered; [cf. 2. चैत्य.]
—चैत्र-
वती, f., N. of a river.
—चैत्र-सख, अस्, m. the
friend of the month Caitra, i. e. the god of love.
—चैत्रावली (˚र-आव्˚), f. the day of full moon in
the month Caitra.

चैत्रक, अस्, m. the month Caitra; (a patronymic
fr. चित्रा.)

चैत्रकूटी, f. (fr. चित्र-कूट), title of a com-
mentary on a grammatical work.

चैत्ररथ, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. चित्र-रथ), treating
of the Gandharva Citra-ratha; (अस्), m. a patronymic
from Citra-ratha; N. of a Dvyaha ceremony; a
facetious expression for the pubes of a woman,
‘Citra-ratha's wood;’ (ई), f. a patronymic of a
daughter of Śaśa-vindu; (अम्), n., scil. वन, the
grove of the deity Kuvera cultivated by the Gan-
dharva Citra-ratha.
चैत्ररथि, इस्, m. a patronymic of Śaśa-vindu.

चैत्ररथ्य, अम्, n. the grove of the deity
Kuvera cultivated by the Gandharva Citra-ratha.

चैत्रवाहनी, f. (fr. चित्र-वाहन), a patronymic
of Citrāṅgadā.

चैत्रायण, a patronymic from Citra; N. of a
place.

चैत्रि, इस्, m. the month Caitra; (a various reading
for चैत्रिन्.)

चैत्रिक, अस्, m. and चैत्रिन्, ई, m. the month
Caitra.
